Create a literary vignette from this scene:
A man misses the bus by a few seconds and watches it pull away while it is raining.

He reached the stop as the doors folded shut. For an instant he was close enough to see the driver's profile and the bright interior reflected in the wet pavement. He raised one hand, too late to mean anything. The bus moved off with a long sigh, throwing a fan of water from its wheels. Rain had darkened his shoulders and begun to creep through one shoe. He lowered his hand and looked at the timetable, though he already knew the next number would not be kind.

Render this scene as short literary prose:
A mother wakes before the rest of the family and drinks coffee alone in the kitchen before dawn.

The house was still dark when she came downstairs, carrying her slippers in one hand so they would not slap against the steps. In the kitchen she switched on only the light above the stove. The coffee machine seemed indecently loud, then fell silent. She sat by the window with both hands around the mug. Beyond the glass, the garden was colourless and indistinct. For ten minutes no one called her name. She drank slowly, watching the first thin light collect along the roofs.

Rewrite this scene as a literary vignette:
Two colleagues remain in an office after everyone else has left. They have disagreed all afternoon and now need to finish the same presentation.

By seven, the office had reduced itself to fluorescent light and the soft rush of the ventilation. Their colleagues' chairs stood empty around them. On the screen, the title slide waited with unreasonable cheerfulness. One corrected a figure; the other changed it back, then paused. Neither referred to the afternoon's argument. They worked through the remaining slides with careful sentences and long stretches of typing. When at last the presentation was saved, they looked at each other briefly, each waiting for the other to decide whether the day was finished.

Turn the following description into a short literary passage:
A teenage boy waits outside a classroom before an exam. He can hear other students talking inside.

He stood beside the classroom door with his notes folded small enough to fit inside one hand. Voices came through the wood in bursts: a formula, somebody laughing, a chair scraped back. He read the first line again and discovered he no longer understood it. Around him, the corridor filled and emptied as students arrived. When the invigilator appeared, he put the notes into his pocket without looking at them once more. The handle turned, and the room beyond seemed suddenly much quieter.

Create a literary vignette from this scene:
A woman waters plants in her father's empty house while he is in hospital. She notices that one plant has begun to flower.

She moved from room to room with the watering can, careful not to spill on the polished floor. The house smelled closed, faintly of dust and his aftershave. On the kitchen sill, the geranium had opened two red flowers since her last visit. She bent toward them with an attention they did not require. Beside the pot stood his reading glasses, one arm folded beneath the other. She watered the soil until it darkened, then wiped a drop from the saucer and left everything else untouched.

Render this scene as short literary prose:
A shop assistant rearranges the same display near closing time because there are no customers.

With ten minutes left, she folded the blue scarf for the third time. The shop had been empty long enough for the music to become noticeable, each song followed by another chosen by no one present. She moved two handbags closer together, stepped back, and moved them apart again. Outside, people passed the window without turning their heads. The till showed the same total it had shown an hour earlier. When the clock finally changed, she straightened a price card and allowed herself to look toward the door.

Rewrite this scene as a literary vignette:
A man arrives home carrying a birthday cake after learning that the person he bought it for will not be coming.

He set the cake on the kitchen table and removed his coat before remembering there was no reason to hurry. The box was tied with white string; a small grease mark had appeared at one corner during the journey home. He put on the kettle, then switched it off before it boiled. The room seemed arranged for an evening that had already been cancelled. After a while he untied the string carefully, not because he wanted cake, but because leaving the box closed felt more deliberate.

Turn the following description into a short literary passage:
A child waits at the window for snow that has been forecast, but the street remains wet and ordinary.

All morning she returned to the window, pressing two fingers against the cold glass. The forecast had promised snow, and she had placed her boots beside the door before breakfast. Outside, cars passed through shallow water and left dark tracks on the road. The sky remained the colour of unwashed wool. Once, she called everyone to look at a pale speck drifting past, but it was only a scrap of paper. By lunchtime the boots were still waiting, upright and hopeful beneath their hooks.

Create a literary vignette from this scene:
A woman sits in a café waiting for an old friend she has not seen in years. The friend is late.

She chose a table from which she could see both the door and the clock above the counter. Her coffee arrived too hot, then became cold while she watched people enter who were not the person she expected. She had imagined the first sentence several times on the way there; now each version seemed unsuitable. At twenty past, she removed her coat. At half past, she put it over the chair beside her. When the door opened again, she looked up before she could decide not to.

Render this scene as short literary prose:
A father repairs a loose bicycle chain in the garage while his daughter waits impatiently to ride.

He turned the bicycle upside down and worked the chain back onto the smallest cog, his fingers quickly blackened with grease. His daughter circled the garage in her helmet, asking whether it was done at intervals that grew shorter each time. He answered without looking up. Outside, sunlight lay across the driveway, bright and usable. At last the wheel spun freely beneath his hand. She was already reaching for the handlebars before he had finished wiping his fingers on the old cloth by the door.
